To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stress distribution is affected by loading direction and implant-abutment connection system.

the stress distribution in bone and prosthetic components of implant-supported partial denture with different implant-abutment connection types (external hexagon (EH), internal hexagon (IH), and Morse taper (MT)) was evaluated using a 3D FE analysis under axial and oblique load conditions.

1) the internal connection system implants present a better stress distribution than the external connection system implants; 2) oblique load increases the stress on bone structures, prosthetic components and abutment screws; 3) internal connection system implants are better than external connection system implants for oblique load; and 4) the stress distribution of internal connection system implants is better than external connection systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stress distribution of implant-supported prostheses under axial and oblique loads.
the stress distribution on the implant, abutment and bone under axial and oblique load.
the development of a numerical method for the simulation of the stress-strain state of the implant and the abutment in a dental implant-supported prosthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress distribution in the implant-abutment connection is dependent on the loading conditions, implant design, and the type of abutment connection.

, for the implants and abutments tested, the external hexagon connection system was more favorable than the internal hexagon connection system, and the internal hexagon and Morse taper connection systems were more favorable than the external hexagon system under oblique loading.
the implant-abutment connection system is a key factor for the success of implant-supported prostheses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stress distribution of internal connection system implants is more favorable for the bone structures and prosthetics than that of external connection system implants.
the internal connections are more favorable than the external ones, but this is only true when the implants are loaded axially.
the implant-abutment connection is the weakest link in the restoration and that the internal connection system is more favorable than the external one.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the internal connection system implants present a better stress distribution pattern under oblique loads than do the external connection system implants and that the internal connection systems are more favorable for the bone structure and prosthetic components.
the internal connection systems are better than the external connection systems for stress distribution.
the stress distribution on the implant and bone is different depending on the type of connection and the type of loading applied.
